issues.body: `write_offset` calls `sync_data` on the temporary file and then renames it, but it does not fsync the parent directory. Persisting file contents does not durably commit the directory-entry creation/replacement; after the function returns successfully, a crash can therefore restore the old watermark or lose the first watermark entirely. That contradicts the public durable-resume contract and can replay broker-confirmed records after restart. The replacement test checks ordinary reopen behavior only and cannot establish crash durability.
issues.fix_hint: After the atomic rename, open and sync the containing directory on platforms that support it, and provide an equivalent platform-specific durability operation or an explicitly documented limitation elsewhere. Factor the sequence into a tested durable-replace helper and add fault/crash-oriented coverage around the post-rename durability boundary; keep the previous valid offset intact on every reported failure.
issues.title: Watermark rename is not made durable in the containing directory

verdict.summary: The prior Windows replacement concern is addressed: Rust's file rename operation supports replacing an existing file on Windows, and the new repeated-watermark test exercises replacement and reopening. However, the implementation still does not satisfy its advertised crash-durable watermark contract. It syncs the temporary file's contents but never syncs the containing directory after the rename, so a successful pump can report and expose an advanced watermark that is lost after a power failure or kernel crash. That can cause already-confirmed broker records to be replayed after restart. This is a new major finding, so progress is regressing.
